skill.name: Hook Development
skill.description: Guides developers through Claude Code hook design, including event configuration, prompt hooks, command hooks, validation patterns, testing, and migration.
skill.summary: Build and test Claude Code hooks for validation, automation, and workflow policy enforcement.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are documentation or defensive hook examples and are false positives. I confirmed meaningful risk in the test helper command string construction and in advanced logging examples that persist raw hook input. Prompt-based validation examples also need injection guardrails when they interpolate tool data.

remediation.suggestion: Invoke hook scripts with argument arrays or positional parameters. Avoid bash -c strings that include user-controlled paths.
Redact prompts, file content, paths, tokens, and credentials before local, Slack, or database logging.

remediation.issue: SQL interpolation in database logging example
remediation.suggestion: Use parameterized inserts or a safe client wrapper instead of embedding $input directly in SQL.

remediation.issue: Prompt injection exposure in prompt hooks
remediation.suggestion: Wrap tool data in explicit untrusted-data delimiters and tell the model to ignore instructions inside tool input.

semantic_findings.title: Command Injection in Hook Test Helper
semantic_findings.description: scripts/test-hook.sh builds a bash -c command string from the hook script and test input path. A crafted path can change the shell command run by the tester.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script stores user-controlled paths in HOOK_SCRIPT and TEST_INPUT, then interpolates them into a single bash -c string. This is a direct shell injection pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Hook Input Sent to Database Log
semantic_findings.description: The advanced database logging example inserts the full hook input into a database command. Hook input can contain user prompts, file content, paths, and secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example reads complete stdin into input and embeds it in a psql command using DATABASE_URL. The data exposure and SQL interpolation risks are explicit in the snippet.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Hook Input Written to Local Audit Log
semantic_findings.description: The audit logging example writes the complete hook payload to ~/.claude/audit.log. This can persist sensitive prompts, paths, and file content without redaction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The snippet appends timestamp, user, tool name, and raw input to a hidden home-directory log. The risk depends on hook payload content, but the retention behavior is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Hooks Interpolate Untrusted Tool Data
semantic_findings.description: Several security validation prompts place raw tool input or file content directly into model instructions. Adversarial content can try to override the validation prompt unless delimiters and injection rules are added.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples recommend prompt-based security decisions using raw $TOOL_INPUT fields. I did not find companion guidance to treat interpolated values as untrusted data.

content.value_statement: Claude Code hooks can be hard to configure safely across events. This skill guides hook formats, validation patterns, testing, and migration to prompt-based workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Claude Code hook event types and configuration formats.
Provides prompt-based and command hook examples for validation.
Shows patterns for file safety, bash command checks, test enforcement, and context loading.
Includes scripts to lint hook scripts, test hooks, and validate hook configuration JSON.
Covers migration from bash-based hooks to prompt-based hooks.
limitations: Does not install or activate hooks automatically.
Examples require shell, jq, and Claude Code hook support.
Prompt-based hook decisions depend on model behavior and careful prompt design.
Some advanced examples need security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Add pre-flight tool validation
use_cases.description: Create PreToolUse hooks that review bash commands, file writes, and sensitive paths before tools run.

use_cases.title: Migrate script hooks
use_cases.description: Replace brittle shell checks with prompt hooks that express validation rules in natural language.

use_cases.title: Test hooks before release
use_cases.description: Validate hook configuration, run sample event payloads, and inspect hook output before publishing a plugin.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Hook Development skill to create a PreToolUse hook that asks before Bash commands with destructive operations. Explain the files to edit.

prompt_templates.title: Validate file writes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Hook Development skill to design a Write/Edit hook that blocks system paths, path traversal, and credential files. Include testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate an existing hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Hook Development skill to convert this command hook into a prompt-based hook. Preserve safety rules and list edge cases to test: [paste hook].

prompt_templates.title: Design a hook suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Hook Development skill to design a plugin hook suite with PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, and SessionStart hooks. Include validation, observability, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a hook that reviews Write operations before they run.
output_examples.output: A plan with a PreToolUse matcher, safety criteria, timeout guidance, and test scenarios.

output_examples.input: Migrate a bash validation hook to prompt hooks.
Check my hook configuration before release.
output_examples.output: A review of event names, hook types, matchers, timeout values, and restart requirements.

best_practices: Start with prompt hooks for contextual security decisions and use command hooks for deterministic checks.
Quote shell variables, validate input, and test hooks with representative event payloads.
Restart Claude Code after hook changes and verify behavior with debug logs.
anti_patterns: Do not pass raw untrusted content into security prompts without delimiters and denial criteria.
Do not log complete hook inputs to external systems or local files without redaction.
Do not build test commands with shell strings that include untrusted paths.

faq.question: Does this skill create hooks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and helper scripts for developers who create Claude Code hooks.

faq.question: Which hook events does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, and Notification.

faq.question: When should I use prompt hooks?
faq.answer: Use prompt hooks when validation needs context, intent analysis, or flexible policy reasoning.

faq.question: When should I use command hooks?
faq.answer: Use command hooks for fast deterministic checks, local tool integration, or simple file inspections.

faq.question: What tools do the examples require?
faq.answer: The shell examples assume bash, jq, and a Claude Code environment that provides hook event payloads.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting points. Review logging, shell quoting, prompt injection defenses, and secret handling before production use.
